findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: Inspector facility to be using a faulty hot holding unit to serve day-old rice. The hot holding unit had been tested 10 days prior (02/07/25) and had been shown to not be holding temperature. Inspector instructed facility to not use the hot holding as a temperature controlled device. Facility agreed on 02/07/25 to use time as control for all rice held in the unit. On 02/17/2025, inspector returned to conduct a follow-up. Upon arrival, the hot holding unit was full of trays of day-old rice, and was still consistently probing below 135F (118-125F). Discussed hot holding procedure with PIC again, who again agreed to throw out the day old rice and use time as control for the rest of the rice in the unit (prepared at 11AM, must be thrown out by 3PM). Ensure that the unit is not used as a temperature controlled device until it can be serviced. Inspector will return 02/26/2025 to re-asses violation.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(I) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (I) EMPLOYEES are properly maintaining the temperatures of TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOODS during hot and cold holding through daily oversight of the EMPLOYEES’ routine monitoring of FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the hot holding unit to be holding temperatures between 118F and 125F (Probed). Facility knew the unit was not holding temperature, but was still using it to store food for more than 4 hours. Discussed with PIC. PIC indicated that the hot holding unit was still waiting to be serviced and should be done by tomorrow (02/18/25). Ensure hot holding unit is serviced to bring temperatures back up to proper holding temperatures. Food may be stored in the unit, but only for 4 HOURS AT A TIME. Because the unit is not measuring 135F, it is no longer considered temperature controlled for safety. Therefore, food stored in unit must be thrown out after 4 hours. Inspector will return 02/26/2025 to re-asses violation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed there to be no sanitizer in any of the 3 sanitizer buckets in the facility (cook line, lobby, and dish room). Discussed with PIC. PIC stated they changed the sanitizer this morning because it was empty, and the buckets must have been filled before it was changed. PIC switched out all sanitizer buckets with fresh sanitizer measuring 200ppm of Quat sanitizer. Ensure that the concentration of sanitizer in the buckets is checked regularly to maintain sanitary food-contact areas.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the hot holding unit used to store fried rice was holding temperatures of 115-120F. Discussed with PIC. PIC stated that they had a suspicion that the hot holding unit was not holding temperature. PIC agreed to use time as control for the 3 trays of rice in the unit. The rice was prepared at 11am, so it must be discarded by 3pm. Ensure that all hot holding units are kept at proper temperature to maintain food safety. Test temperature regularly to ensure this is happening. Inspector will return 02/17/2025 to re-assess this violation.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: 2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
All sanitizer buckets were at 100ppm (q) at time of inspection. Discussed with PIC, all buckets were changed and measured 200ppm (q). Ensure that sanitizer buckets are changed frequently so that the concentration stays at 200ppm for proper sanitation(q).  

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Areas in need of caulk include:
-Area around mop sink
-Area above the 3 part sink
-(NEW) Men’s restroom sink
-(NEW) Two back prep sinks 
Discussed with PIC.  Ensure these areas are caulked to prevent accumulation of moisture and debris, resulting in mold growth.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
A coving tile located to the left of the cash register is missing.  Discussed with PIC.  Floor and wall juncture shall be coved to create a smooth, non-absorbent, easily cleanable surface.  Ensure coving tile is replaced.

6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.
